content.content:
# The security team's handbook. It sits inside the engineering handbook's
# content root, but it's a project of its own, with its own content model: the
# handbook's checks, builds, and language server leave these files to it.
spec = "0.1"

[project]
content-root = "content"
output-dir = ".ascribe/build"

[types.page]
default = true

[types.page.frontmatter]
title = "string"
description = { type = "string?", role = "description" }

# Policies record who owns them, how often they're reviewed, and since when
# they apply. `ascribe report inventory` counts them by owner.
[types.policy]
files = ["policies/**"]

[types.policy.frontmatter]
title = "string"
owner = { type = "string", role = "owner" }
review = "enum(quarterly, yearly)"
effective = "date"
# The next review is due by this date; `review-overdue` reports a policy
# whose date has passed.
review-by = { type = "date?", role = "review-date" }

[notes.policy]
label = "Policy"

[phrases]
team = "Security"
channel = "#security"
report = "security@lantern.example"

# Severity names are case-sensitive, so "sev1" in a URL isn't linked.
[glossary]
case-sensitive = true

[glossary.terms.sev1]
term = "SEV1"
definition = "An incident with customer data exposed or the service down for everyone."
link = "/incident-response.md#severity-levels"

[glossary.terms.sev2]
term = "SEV2"
definition = "An incident that degrades the service for some customers, with no data exposed."
link = "/incident-response.md#severity-levels"
---
# Content model

## Page types

- `page` (the default): frontmatter `title` (string, required), `description` (string)
- `policy` (files `policies/**`): frontmatter `title` (string, required), `owner` (string, required), `review` (enum(quarterly, yearly), required), `effective` (date, required), `review-by` (date)

## Phrases

- `{team}`: Security
- `{channel}`: #security
- `{report}`: security@lantern.example

## Glossary

- `sev1`: SEV1
- `sev2`: SEV2

## Builds

- `site`, the editor's build: variants switch, availability badge
---
---
title: Secrets
owner: security
review: yearly
effective: 2025-09-01
review-by: 2030-09-01
---

Secrets are passwords, API keys, tokens, and private keys: anything that grants access if someone else has it.

@note {type=policy}
Secrets never go in source code, chat, or tickets. Store them in the secrets manager, and read them at runtime.

## If a secret leaks
@id: if-a-secret-leaks

Treat it as an incident, at least SEV2. Rotate the secret first, then report it to {channel}: a leaked secret that's already rotated is a much smaller problem.

## Rotation
@id: rotation

Rotate every secret at least once a year, and whenever someone who knew it leaves the team.
---
---
title: Security handbook
description: How the security team protects Lantern and its customers.
---

The {team} team keeps Lantern and its customers' data safe. This handbook is for every engineer, not only the {team} team.

## Report a problem
@id: report

@include: _fragments/report.md

## Policies
@id: policies

- [](policies/access-reviews.md)
- [](policies/secrets.md)

## Incidents
@id: incidents

[](incident-response.md) says what happens after a report, and who does what.

Write a new page of type `policy` titled "Laptops".

Where: in the content root, `handbook/pages/security/content/`, at a path matching `policies/**` (relative to it).
Project: handbook/pages/security/

Start the file with this frontmatter, and fill in each `…`:
```yaml
---
title: "Laptops"
owner: …

---
```
The type's fields:
- `title` (string, required)
- `owner` (string, required)
- `review` (enum(quarterly, yearly), required)
- `effective` (date, required)
- `review-by` (date)
A file or folder whose name starts with `_` is a fragment, not a page: don't name the page that way.

When you're done, run `ascribe check handbook/pages/security/content` and fix what it reports.
---
---
title: Access reviews
owner: security
review: quarterly
effective: 2026-01-15
review-by: 2030-01-15
---

Every quarter, each team lead reviews who has access to their team's systems, and removes access nobody needs.

@note {type=policy}
Access that isn't confirmed in a review is removed two weeks after the review closes.

## What's reviewed
@id: whats-reviewed

- Production databases and their backups.
- Cloud accounts and their admin roles.
- The deploy dashboard.

## How to review
@id: how-to-review

@steps
1. Open the review issue the {team} team files for your team.
2. For each person, confirm the access, reduce it, or remove it.
3. Close the issue. The {team} team applies the changes.
---
Email {report} or post in {channel}. Say what you saw and when; don't try to confirm it yourself first. For anything urgent outside working hours, page the {team} on-call.
---
---
title: Incident response
description: What happens when something goes wrong, from the first report to the review.
---

An incident is anything that may expose customer data or take the service down. When in doubt, call it an incident: closing one costs nothing.

## Severity levels
@id: severity-levels

| Level | Meaning | Response |
|---|---|---|
| SEV1 | Customer data exposed, or the service down for everyone. | Page the {team} lead at once, day or night. |
| SEV2 | The service degraded for some customers, no data exposed. | Respond within an hour, in working hours. |
| SEV3 | A problem with no customer impact yet. | Fix it in the normal course of work. |

## During an incident
@id: during

@steps
1. Name one incident lead. They decide; everyone else helps.
2. Open a channel for the incident, and post updates there every 30 minutes.
3. Contain first: rotate leaked secrets, block the attacker, turn off the feature.
4. Only then investigate and fix the cause.

@note {type=caution}
Don't delete logs or data during an incident, even to contain it. We need them to find out what happened.

## After an incident
@id: after

Every SEV1 and SEV2 gets a written review within five working days. Reviews are blameless: they ask what made the mistake easy, not who made it.

.The review template
@details:
- What happened, with a timeline.
- What the impact was, and on whom.
- What we did, and what worked.
- What we'll change, with an owner and a date for each change.
@end

# Laptops

A laptop holds source code, credentials, and sessions that are already signed in. This policy covers every laptop used for Lantern work.

> **Policy**
>
> Every laptop has an encrypted disk and a screen that locks after five minutes. A lost laptop is reported within an hour.

## Disk encryption

Encrypt the laptop's whole disk. An encrypted disk can't be read by someone who has the laptop but not your password.

## Screen lock

Set the screen to lock after five minutes without use, and to ask for your password to unlock.

## If a laptop is lost

Report a lost or stolen laptop within an hour of noticing it's gone, at any time of day.

Email security@lantern.example or post in #security. Say what you saw and when; don't try to confirm it yourself first. For anything urgent outside working hours, page the Security on-call.
